title: Core load validation pins the canon 4/8/16 junction ladder using a render justification, coupling catalog extensibility to a core edit
detail: Pipe tiers validate generic sim constraints (capacity > 0); junctions instead pin the current roster ladder, justified by render geometry (the LED ring) — a presentation concern reaching into core. A future canon tier (the pipe ladder already lists a Backbone 4th tier) requires a core code edit, not data-only, and the ladder is restated again in view.odin's router_tier_scale switch.
recommended_fix: Validate the sim-generic domain in core (junction port_capacity > 0 — 0=unlimited is terminal-only) and enforce the canon ladder via content review, or explicitly tag the check as canon-locked.

title: draw_router outer-ring comments describe a geometry the code does not implement (offset is +4 = 90°, not 180°, and both rings cover every angle)
detail: The only case reaching this branch is port_capacity=16 → leds=16 → stride=1, so the outer offset is 4 positions = 90°, not 180°. With 16 LEDs each ring occupies all 16 angles: every angle renders two LEDs (inner + outer) — a concentric double ring, never the described alternation. Misleading comments will mislead future tier tuning.
recommended_fix: Correct the comments to describe the actual geometry: outer ring offset +4 (90°), producing a concentric double light ring at every angle (the look-book read).
